Predict Function for communityPGLMM Model Objects

Source: R/pglmm-utils.R
predict.communityPGLMM.Rd

Predicted values of a fitted model, for the data used to fit the model or for new data.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'communityPGLMM'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  re.form = NULL,
  type = c("link", "response"),
  allow.new.levels = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted model with class communityPGLMM.

newdata

An optional data frame with the predictors (and the grouping variables of random terms, unless re.form is NA or ~0) to predict with. The response is not needed. If NULL (default), predictions are for the data used to fit the model, see pglmm_predicted_values().

re.form

(formula, NULL, or NA) specify which random effects to condition on when predicting. If NULL, include all random effects (i.e Xb + Zu); if NA or ~0, include no random effects (i.e. Xb).

type

Whether the predicted values are on the scale of the linear predictor ("link", default) or of the response ("response").

allow.new.levels

Whether to allow levels of grouping variables in newdata that were not in the data used to fit the model. If TRUE, their random effects are set to zero; if FALSE (default), they give an error. Only used with newdata.

...

Additional arguments passed to pglmm_predicted_values() when newdata is NULL, e.g. gaussian.pred.

Value

A matrix with one column (Y_hat) and one row for each row of the data (or of newdata). Rows of newdata with missing values in the variables needed have NA.

Details

With newdata, the predicted values are the fixed part (Xb) calculated with the predictors in newdata, plus (unless re.form is NA or ~0) the estimates of the random effects (see ranef()) of the levels of the grouping variables in newdata:

  • For phylogenetic terms such as (1 | sp__), the estimates of both the non-phylogenetic and the phylogenetic random terms are added.

  • For random slopes such as (x | sp), the estimates are multiplied by the values of x in newdata.

  • For nested terms such as (1 | sp__@site), the estimates are those of the combinations of levels (e.g. of sp and site) in newdata.

  • Levels (or combinations of levels for nested terms) that were not in the data used to fit the model have no estimate. They give an error, unless allow.new.levels = TRUE, in which case their random effects are set to zero (the predictions for them are then unconditional on these random terms). This also applies to species that are in the phylogeny but not in the data used to fit the model.

  • The observation-level random term (1|obs), which is added by default for poisson and binomial (with more than one trial) models, is always set to zero, as the rows of newdata are treated as new observations. As a result, for these models, predictions with newdata being the data used to fit the model are different from those without newdata.

For models fitted with bayes = TRUE, predictions with newdata are calculated in the same way, with the posterior summaries (see marginal.summ of pglmm()) of fixed and random effects. They have no credible intervals.

Predictions with newdata and random effects are only available for models with random terms specified in the formula (i.e. not via the argument random.effects of pglmm()).

Examples

# community data: abundance of each species at each site
dat <- data.frame(
  site = rep(rownames(comm_a), times = ncol(comm_a)),
  sp = rep(colnames(comm_a), each = nrow(comm_a)),
  freq = unlist(comm_a, use.names = FALSE)
)
dat$shade <- envi$shade[match(dat$site, envi$site)]
phy <- ape::keep.tip(phylotree, unique(dat$sp))
fit <- pglmm(freq ~ shade + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site),
  data = dat, cov_ranef = list(sp = phy)
)

# predictions for the data used to fit the model
head(predict(fit))
#>         Y_hat
#> [1,] 2.884917
#> [2,] 3.434059
#> [3,] 3.747206
#> [4,] 2.857687
#> [5,] 3.695014
#> [6,] 4.384845

# predictions for new data: the response is not needed
newdat <- data.frame(
  sp = c("Acer_rubrum", "Acer_rubrum", "Achillea_millefolium"),
  site = c("s3293", "s3294", "s3293"),
  shade = c(20, 50, 80)
)
predict(fit, newdata = newdat)
#>      Y_hat
#> 1 2.864494
#> 2 3.545248
#> 3 1.319520
# without random effects (the grouping variables are then not needed)
predict(fit, newdata = newdat, re.form = NA)
#>       Y_hat
#> 1 0.1816630
#> 2 0.8624171
#> 3 1.5431712

# a site (or species) that was not in the data used to fit the model gives
# an error, unless allow.new.levels = TRUE: its random effect is then zero
newdat2 <- data.frame(sp = "Acer_rubrum", site = "a_new_site", shade = 50)
predict(fit, newdata = newdat2, allow.new.levels = TRUE)
#>      Y_hat
#> 1 3.545248

# binomial model: predicted probabilities
dat$pa <- as.numeric(dat$freq > 0)
fit_pa <- pglmm(pa ~ shade + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site),
  data = dat, family = "binomial", cov_ranef = list(sp = phy)
)
predict(fit_pa, newdata = newdat, type = "response")
#>       Y_hat
#> 1 0.3594783
#> 2 0.4820189
#> 3 0.4002902
